Where this comes from
This planner covers the whole US. Park types, official websites and how you can activate come from POTA’s park list, refreshed every week; campgrounds and picnic shelters come from Recreation.gov (federal land only, so check state parks on their own site; camping info last checked by date on each file); SOTA summits come from SOTA and WWFF references from the WWFF directory. Boundaries on the map are the official USGS PAD-US outlines; when a park has none, its outline is from OpenStreetMap and is labelled “OpenStreetMap outline (unofficial)”. For Kentucky, the full KPC Trip Planner adds hand-checked access points, plus 2-fer research and more. Place search by OpenStreetMap Nominatim. Routes open in Google Maps.
We’re volunteers working from public maps, and we make mistakes. Before you activate, check the official park map, make sure the land is public and open, and follow each program’s rules. Your activation is your responsibility. See something wrong? Let us know.
⚠️ Parks' boundaries may overlap here, but we can't confirm it. Check both official boundary maps and make your own call before you count it.
